name: Classic Maya Script
notes: Region-level Mesoamerican writing has a strong claim to having developed with no Old World contact (INDEPENDENT at the macro level), but which Mesoamerican tradition (Olmec/Cascajal, Zapotec, Epi-Olmec/Isthmian) gave rise to Maya script specifically is unresolved — the 2005-2006 San Bartolo discovery shows a mature script by c. 300-200 BCE with no obvious transitional forms linking back to Olmec symbols, leading some scholars to treat Maya writing as a plausibly separate "homegrown" development. origin_type is coded UNCERTAIN at the system-derivation level; see claim_maya_origin_type. `latest: null` because a form of the script remains in ceremonial/decorative use and Mayan languages are still spoken, though the classic logosyllabic writing system itself fell out of common use after the Spanish conquest.
